walkthroughs.body_html:
Water — a core area of GCSE Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Water brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Water.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Evaporation
Transpiration
Condensation
Sublimation
Evaporation
Condensation
Precipitation
Run-off
Water flowing through soil into rivers.
Water vapour released from plant leaves to the atmosphere.
Water bubbling up from underground.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
